newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Finmin sees lower interest rates in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Finmin sees lower interest rates in 1997.

text.p: Portugal's Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said that interest rates should fall steadily in 1997 and the spread between Portuguese and German rates should continue to narrow.
"I believe the conditions are there for a bigger cut in the spreads (with Germany) and a steady continuation in the trend to lower interest rates," Sousa Franco said.

The temporary reversal of the trend in January had been due to some "unfortunate" political statements that had had a negative impact on the markets, he said in reference to remarks by some northern European political leaders about the wisdom of southern European countries joining the single currency.
"The situation is returning to normal," he added.
The spread between Portugal's benchmark 10-year bond and the Bund equivalent is around 112 basis points against a low of 80 basis points reached earlier in January.
